newsitem.title: USA: Lennar sees record 1997 revs and net income.
newsitem.headline: Lennar sees record 1997 revs and net income.

text.p: Lennar Corp said Thursday it expects to achieve record revenues and net earnings for 1997.
The First Call consensus earnings per share estimate for the year is $2.82. Lennar's 1997 second quarter earnings of $0.61 per share beat Wall Street estimates by $0.05 per share.

"As we pass the mid-point of this current year, it is evident that Lennar should achieve another record year in 1997," company president and chief executive officer Stuart Miller said in a press release.

Miller said the anticipated strong performance is being led by a combination of factors, including record sales and earnings through the first six months of the year, margins that continue to exceed historic levels, and Lennar's plans to spin-off its asset management business and merge with Pacific Greystone Corp.
Recently added homebuilding operations in California also will contribute significantly to second half results, he said.

Vice president for finannce Cory Boydston would not offer an earnings estimate, but said "It shouldn't be a problem" beating last year's results. In 1996, the company recorded net earings of $87.99 million or $2.43 per share on revenues of more than $1.18 billion.
